evidence_frontier: The latest completed w8 confirmation (PNN-v1-W8-Confirmation) trained Alpha5 w8 and the Alpha5 w16 control for 50 epochs on ECG200, yielding aggregate Q.ANT correct counts 424/500 vs 441/500, failing the relative gate (candidate_correct >= control_correct - 10). Earlier experiments (Exp020) showed Alpha5 w16 achieving 897/1000 correct on ECG200 after promotion, and Exp021 showed w8 at 887/1000 correct after 100‑epoch training on the full 100‑sample train set, but that result used a different seed set and was not a preregistered confirmation. The evidence indicates a persistent performance gap at 50 epochs that may shrink with longer training.
analysis: Observation: At 50 epochs, Alpha5 w8 underperforms the w16 control by 17 correct predictions (424 vs 441) on 500 aggregated predictions, violating the relative gate. Hypothesis: Extending training to 100 epochs will allow the narrower w8 model to close this gap, potentially achieving performance within 10 correct predictions of the w16 control under the same seed set and data split.
hypothesis: Training Alpha5 with local_width=8 for 100 epochs will improve its aggregate correct predictions on ECG200 such that candidate_correct >= control_correct - 10 when evaluated on the same fresh seed set and test split.

proposal.title: 100‑Epoch w8 Confirmation on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Does extending training to 100 epochs enable the Alpha5 w8 model to meet the relative performance gate against the Alpha5 w16 control on ECG200?
proposal.rationale: The 50‑epoch w8 confirmation showed a 17‑prediction deficit relative to w16. Prior longer‑training runs (e.g., Exp021) suggest that additional epochs can boost w8 performance. Testing the preregistered gate with 100 epochs will determine if the w8 boundary can be confirmed without altering architecture.

procedure: For each seed, train Alpha5 w8 and the concurrent Alpha5 w16 control on the ECG200 TRAIN split (100 samples) for exactly 100 epochs using identical hyperparameters.
After training, evaluate each model on the ECG200 TEST split (100 samples) and record the number of correct Q.ANT predictions per seed.
Aggregate the correct counts across the 5 seeds to obtain 500 total predictions per model.
Apply the relative gate: candidate_correct must be at least control_correct minus 10.

proposal.success_criteria: candidate_correct >= control_correct - 10 on 500 predictions (5 seeds × 100 test samples).
proposal.risks: Longer training may lead to over‑fitting on the small ECG200 train set, increasing variance across seeds. Simulation noise could obscure true performance differences. The gate margin is tight; random fluctuations might cause a false negative.
